newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris Club agrees debt relief for Ethiopia.
newsitem.headline: Paris Club agrees debt relief for Ethiopia.

text.p: The Paris Club of creditor nations said on Friday it had agreed to give debt relief to Ethiopia, giving the African country the most generous terms of debt reduction currently available to the world's poorest nations.

The agreement, which follows an accord with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) on economic reforms, allows reduction on debt repayments of up to 67 percent, under so-called "Naples terms" of debt relief.
They could also undertake debt for nature, debt for aid, debt for equity swaps or local currency swaps on up to 20 percent of the debt concerned, the Paris Club said in a statement.
Creditor countries agreed they could meet by the end of 1999 to consider any reduction in the stock of debt.
Naples terms allow for a 67-percent reduction on either the stock of debt or on payments due.

The Paris Club is considering providing more generous debt relief for the world's poorest nations under an agreement reached last year for joint action between the national creditors, the IMF and the World Bank.
It has not yet offered these enhanced terms, which could involve debt reduction of up to 80 percent to countries which have already completed a three-year IMF-approved economic reform programme.
